war-2025-2026.note: He continued to run occupied Crimea.

war-2025-2026.name: Refat Chubarov
war-2025-2026.note: He led the Mejlis from mainland Ukraine, barred from Crimea by Russian authorities.

national-revival.name: Pyotr Schmidt
national-revival.note: He led the Sevastopol uprising of November 1905 and was executed in 1906.

national-revival.name: Grigoriy Chukhnin
national-revival.note: As Black Sea Fleet commander he put down the 1905 mutinies and was killed in 1906.

national-revival.name: Alexander Kolchak
national-revival.note: He commanded the Black Sea Fleet at Sevastopol from 1916 until 1917.

ukrainian-revolution.name: Mikhail Sablin
ukrainian-revolution.note: The Sevastopol-born commander raised the Ukrainian flag on the fleet in April 1918.

ukrainian-revolution.name: Yuri Gaven
ukrainian-revolution.note: The Latvian revolutionary was sent to Sevastopol in 1917 and helped organise the seizure of power in Crimea.

soviet-takeover.name: Pyotr Wrangel
soviet-takeover.note: He ruled from Sevastopol in 1920 and organised the evacuation of his army in November.

soviet-takeover.name: Ivan Papanin
soviet-takeover.note: The Sevastopol-born future polar explorer was sent to Crimea in 1920 to organise partisans against Wrangel.

soviet-ukraine-1920s.name: Ivan Yumashev
soviet-ukraine-1920s.note: He commanded the Black Sea destroyer Dzerzhinsky from 1927 to 1931.

holodomor-terror.name: Nikolai Kuznetsov
holodomor-terror.note: He commanded the Black Sea cruiser Chervona Ukraina in 1933-1936.

holodomor-terror.name: Ivan Yumashev
holodomor-terror.note: He commanded the Black Sea Fleet in 1938-1939, during the purges of its leadership.

soviet-annexations.name: Filipp Oktyabrsky
soviet-annexations.note: He took command of the fleet in March 1939.

soviet-annexations.name: Nikolai Kulakov
soviet-annexations.note: He sat on the Black Sea Fleet's Military Council at the outbreak of war in 1941.

nazi-occupation.name: Ivan Petrov
nazi-occupation.note: He commanded the Separate Coastal Army in the defence of Sevastopol.

nazi-occupation.name: Lyudmila Pavlichenko
nazi-occupation.note: She fought at Odesa and Sevastopol, where she was wounded in 1942.

nazi-occupation.name: Nina Onilova
nazi-occupation.note: She was mortally wounded in the fighting for Sevastopol in March 1942.

nazi-occupation.name: Erwin Jaenecke
nazi-occupation.note: He commanded the 17th Army trapped in Crimea in 1944.

postwar-ussr.name: Filipp Oktyabrsky
postwar-ussr.note: He commanded the fleet again in the rebuilding years to 1948.

postwar-ussr.name: Sergey Gorshkov
postwar-ussr.note: He took command of the Black Sea Fleet in August 1951.

soviet-ukraine-late.name: Mikhail Khronopulo
soviet-ukraine-late.note: He was the penultimate commander of the Soviet Black Sea Fleet.

soviet-ukraine-late.name: Lyudmila Aksyonova
soviet-ukraine-late.note: The Sevastopol-born 400 m runner won Olympic team bronze in 1976.

soviet-ukraine-late.name: Aleksandr Nosatov
soviet-ukraine-late.note: The Sevastopol-born officer began his Soviet Navy career in this period.

independence.name: Boris Kozhin
independence.note: He commanded the new navy from April 1992 to October 1993.

independence.name: Mykhailo Yezhel
independence.note: He led the navy from 1996 to 2003.

orange-to-euromaidan.name: Serhiy Kunitsyn
orange-to-euromaidan.note: He headed the city administration from 2006 to 2010.

orange-to-euromaidan.name: Valeriy Saratov
orange-to-euromaidan.note: The Party of Regions politician held the post from 2010 to 2011.

orange-to-euromaidan.name: Volodymyr Yatsuba
orange-to-euromaidan.note: He held the post from 2011 until the events of 2014.

orange-to-euromaidan.name: Aleksandr Vitko
orange-to-euromaidan.note: He took command of the fleet in April 2013.

crimea-donbas-war.name: Aleksei Chaly
crimea-donbas-war.note: A rally proclaimed him 'people's mayor' in February 2014 and he then led the Russian-installed assembly.

crimea-donbas-war.name: Serhiy Hayduk
crimea-donbas-war.note: He was named navy commander in March 2014 and was detained by pro-Russian forces in Sevastopol that month.

crimea-donbas-war.name: Denis Berezovsky
crimea-donbas-war.note: He switched allegiance to Russia days after being made navy commander in 2014.

crimea-donbas-war.name: Dmitry Ovsyannikov
crimea-donbas-war.note: He held the post from 2017 to 2019.

full-scale-invasion.name: Mikhail Razvozhayev
full-scale-invasion.note: He has run occupied Sevastopol since 2020.

full-scale-invasion.name: Igor Osipov
full-scale-invasion.note: He commanded the fleet in the opening stage of the invasion, including the loss of the Moskva.

full-scale-invasion.name: Viktor Sokolov
full-scale-invasion.note: He took over the fleet in August 2022.

war-of-attrition.name: Sergei Pinchuk
war-of-attrition.note: The Sevastopol-born admiral took command in 2024 after Ukrainian strikes on the fleet.

war-of-attrition.name: Mikhail Razvozhayev
war-of-attrition.note: He ran the city through repeated Ukrainian strikes on the port.

war-2025-2026.name: Mikhail Razvozhayev
war-2025-2026.note: He continued to administer occupied Sevastopol.

war-2025-2026.name: Sergei Pinchuk
war-2025-2026.note: He continued to command the fleet; press reports in 2025 of his removal were not confirmed.
